segments.text: This is an extreme hidden competition show with a $100,000 prize, where six elite experts
must hide inside an abandoned courthouse, and if they avoid being found for one hour,
they win.
At first, they get three days to study the building and build their hiding spots.
The first player, Alex, chooses a cabinet, and it sounds obvious, but the cabinet actually
has two levels.
He reconstructs the whole thing, lowering the upper compartment by 1.6 feet and creates
a hidden door at the bottom.
Even if the hunter opens it, he'll see nothing wrong.
Sam refuses to hide inside the main building.
He targets the entrance gate because between the walls there's a narrow space that perfectly
follows the rules, and it's the last place the Hunter would ever check.
Tony decides to go underground.
He installs a custom-made marble step.
In previous seasons, the Hunter knocked on floors to detect hollow spaces, so Tony used
thick marble that absorbs sound and made the perfect silent bunker.
Max is the craziest because he notices the production team always sets up a control
room where hiding is forbidden, and the Hunter never looks there, so he spends two and a
half days building an entire fake studio design, even with the fake staff.
Jack discovers a secret office door during scouting, but it's not safe enough, so he
hires a renovation team, transforms the whole wall, adds golden frames, and camouflages the
door so perfectly, you'd swear it was always there.
Chris uses the courtroom furniture, he rebuilds a door with a small hole at the bottom, then
brings a full row of folding chairs to block the opening.
When the chairs fold, the hole becomes completely invisible.
These hiding spots are insane, but will the hunter find the hiding experts?
The countdown starts.
The hunter enters through the courthouse doors and he doesn't even consider the entrance,
meaning Sam is safe.
He taps statues and walls to detect hollows.
Tony's thick marble floor gives him nothing.
Then he reaches Max's fake studio.
At first, he only planned to greet the staff,
but then he notices something strange.
He doesn't recognize any of the cameramen.
